Hoary
HOR-ee
adjective
From the Old English hār, “grey, venerable, old,” whence also hoar (as in hoar-frost); hence white or grey with age. The hoary head is the head grown white with years.

Biblical Definition

Hoary means white or grey with age — the same word that names the hoar-frost lying white upon the ground names the head grown white with years. Scripture never treats that whiteness as a defect. The law commands a posture toward it: “Thou shalt rise up before the hoary head, and honour the face of the old man, and fear thy God: I am the LORD” (Lev 19:32). Mark the yoking of the two commands. To rise when age enters the room and to fear God are set in one breath, for the honour paid to grey hairs is honour paid to the God who gave them; a man who will not stand for the aged has already sat down before his Maker. Solomon adds the crown: “The hoary head is a crown of glory, if it be found in the way of righteousness” (Pro 16:31). The condition is not idle. Grey hairs are a crown, but a crown of glory only where the years have been spent in the way of righteousness; a long life of sin whitens the head without adorning it, and David could charge Solomon to bring Shimei’s hoar head down to the grave with blood (1Ki 2:9). So the word holds both an honour and a warning: the beauty of old men is the gray head (Pro 20:29), and the fifth commandment reaches from a child’s father to every white head in Israel.

Webster 1828 Definition

White or grey with age; the hoary head is the head grown white with years, a crown of glory in the way of righteousness.

HOARY, white or whitish; grey with age; the same word as hoar, of frost.

From the Saxon hār, “grey, venerable, old.”

The hoary head is the head made white by many years.

Israel was commanded to rise up before it and fear God (Lev 19:32).

It is a crown of glory, if found in the way of righteousness (Pro 16:31).

Key Scripture

Lev 19:32 — "Thou shalt rise up before the hoary head, and honour the face of the old man, and fear thy God: I am the LORD."

Pro 16:31 — "The hoary head is a crown of glory, if it be found in the way of righteousness."

Pro 20:29 — "The glory of young men is their strength: and the beauty of old men is the gray head."

1Ki 2:6 — "Do therefore according to thy wisdom, and let not his hoar head go down to the grave in peace."

Modern Corruption

A live corruption: an age that worships youth has emptied the fifth commandment of the honour Scripture commands toward every hoary head.

expand to see more

The corruption here is a settled contempt, and it is everywhere. The age worships youth, prices the old out of usefulness, warehouses them where they will not be seen, and jokes at the white head as though decay were a failure of will. Its whole vocabulary is against the hoary head: the new is progress, the old is out of date, and a man is finished when his strength goes. Scripture commands the opposite posture, and commands it as an act of worship: “Thou shalt rise up before the hoary head, and honour the face of the old man, and fear thy God.” The honour and the fear are one command. He who despises the grey head despises the God who whitened it, and the fifth commandment is not satisfied by tenderness to one’s own parents while every other aged saint is passed by.

But the honour is not flattery, and Solomon guards it with a condition. The hoary head is a crown of glory — if it be found in the way of righteousness. Years alone confer nothing; a man may grow old in folly and carry a white crown upon an empty head, and David could bid Solomon bring Shimei’s hoar head down to the grave with blood. So the word speaks to both ends of life. To the young it says, rise up, uncover, and learn; the beauty of old men is the gray head, and the strength you glory in will be gone in forty years. To the old it says, the crown is given to a life spent in the way of righteousness — therefore finish well, that the whiteness upon your head may be a glory and not a reproach.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

The word means white or grey with age — the head made white by many years.

expand to see more

Hoary — Old English hār, “grey, venerable, old.”

The same root gives hoar, as in hoar-frost lying white upon the ground.

It describes the head whitened by age, and the man who bears it.

Israel must rise before the hoary head and fear God (Lev 19:32).

It is a crown of glory only in the way of righteousness (Pro 16:31).

Usage

"Rise up before the hoary head and fear thy God: the honour and the fear are one command."

"The hoary head is a crown of glory, if it be found in the way of righteousness — not otherwise."

"The glory of young men is their strength; the beauty of old men is the gray head."
